question.body:
#image("/imgs/ap-calc-bc-1999-frq-05-bc-1999_fig3.jpg", width: 55%)

The graph of $f$ consists of three line segments. Let $g(x)=integral_1^x f(t) dif t$.

(a) Compute $g(4)$ and $g(-2)$.

(b) Find $g'(1)$.

(c) Find the absolute minimum of $g$ on $[-2,4]$ and justify.

(d) $g''$ is undefined at $x=1$ and $x=2$. Which of these are inflection points of $g$? Justify.
question.solution:
(a) From signed areas,
$g(4)=3/2+1+1/2-1/2=5/2$, and
$g(-2)=-1/2(12)=-6$.

(b) By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, $g'(1)=f(1)=4$.

(c) Since $g'=f$, $g$ increases on $[-2,3]$ and decreases on $[3,4]$. The minimum is therefore at an endpoint. Since $g(-2)=-6<5/2=g(4)$, the absolute minimum is $-6$.

(d) Only $x=1$. Because $g''=f'$, its sign changes from positive on $(-2,1)$ to negative on $(1,2)$, but remains negative on both sides of $x=2$.
